Module org.slb4j
Package org.slb4j.layout

Class PatternLayout

java.lang.Object
org.slb4j.layout.PatternLayout
All Implemented Interfaces:
LogLayout
public final class PatternLayout extends Object implements LogLayout
The StandardLogPattern class handles the formatting of log entries using Log4J-style format strings.

      Example output: 

       2026-01-11 15:19:09.532 TRACE com.example.Application - Message from JUL
 2026-01-11 15:19:09.540 DEBUG com.example.Application - Message from JCL
 2026-01-11 15:19:09.568 WARN  com.example.Application - Message from Log4j
 2026-01-11 15:19:09.573 INFO  com.example.Application - Message from SLF4J

    • LAYOUT_INSTANCE_COMPACT

      public static final PatternLayout LAYOUT_INSTANCE_COMPACT
      A compact log pattern used to format log entries in a concise and structured manner. The pattern defines the format of log messages by specifying placeholders, alignment, truncation, and other layout options.

      Pattern description:

      • `%highlight{...}`: Highlights the enclosed pattern with console color codes (if isSupported by the logging system).
      • `%d{HH:mm:ss.SSS}`: The timestamp of the log entry without the date.
      • `%-5level`: The log level, left-aligned with a width of 5 characters.
      • `%-30.30c{1.}`: The logger name, left-aligned and truncated to a maximum of 30 characters, showing only the first fragment of the name.
      • `%msg`: The log message.
      • `%n`: A new line character.
      Use when a compact and human-readable log format is preferred, such as console-based logging.

    • LAYOUT_INSTANCE_DETAILED

      public static final PatternLayout LAYOUT_INSTANCE_DETAILED
      A predefined LogLayout instance representing a detailed log format.

      The format includes the following components:

      • Timestamp in the format yyyy-MM-dd HH:mm:ss.SSS
      • Thread name enclosed in square brackets
      • Log level with a minimum width of 5 characters
      • Marker, if present
      • Logger name truncated to a maximum of 36 characters
      • Mapped Diagnostic Context (MDC) key-value pairs enclosed in square brackets
      • Fully qualified class name, method name, file name, and line number
      • Log message
      • Throwable stack trace (if any)
      This format provides comprehensive information about log events, including contextual details, useful for debugging and auditing purposes.

    • parseLog4jPatternString

      public static PatternLayout.LogPatternEntry[] parseLog4jPatternString(String pattern)
      Parses a Log4J-style pattern string and converts it into a list of LogPatternEntry instances, which can be used to format log entries according to the specified pattern.

      Supported pattern specifiers include literals, placeholders for log levels, messages, loggers, etc., as well as specific options for alignment and truncation.

      Parameters:
      pattern - the pattern string in Log4J style, which may include placeholders and literals
      Returns:
      an array of LogPatternEntry instances representing the parsed pattern
